meta.title: Landmark referendums
sources: Result and turnout figures as reported by Wikipedia's referendum articles
meta.note: A curated selection of nationally significant referendums, not an exhaustive list. Managed and sham votes carry caveats.

referendums.name: Indigenous Voice to Parliament
referendums.outcome: The constitutional amendment failed in every state.

referendums.name: Draft constitution
referendums.outcome: The proposed text was rejected on compulsory turnout.

referendums.name: End of Life Choice Act
referendums.outcome: Assisted dying became law in 2021; a cannabis referendum the same day failed 50.7–48.4.

referendums.name: New constitution
referendums.outcome: A landslide to replace the Pinochet-era constitution.

referendums.name: Constitutional amendments
referendums.outcome: Reset Putin's term clock to allow rule to 2036.
referendums.caveat: A managed, week-long plebiscite; the announced figures are recorded as announcements.

referendums.name: Repeal the Eighth Amendment
referendums.outcome: Ended the constitutional abortion ban.

referendums.name: Same-sex marriage postal survey
referendums.outcome: A voluntary postal survey; Parliament legislated marriage equality within weeks.
referendums.caveat: A voluntary survey rather than a binding referendum.

referendums.name: Executive presidency
referendums.outcome: Replaced parliamentary government with the presidential system used since 2018.
referendums.caveat: Held under a state of emergency; observers cited an unlevel field.

referendums.name: EU membership (Brexit)
referendums.outcome: The UK voted to leave the European Union; it withdrew in January 2020.

referendums.name: EU–Ukraine Association Agreement
referendums.outcome: An advisory No on low turnout; the agreement was later ratified with addenda.

referendums.name: Constitutional reform
referendums.outcome: Renzi's reform was crushed; he resigned that night.

referendums.name: FARC peace deal
referendums.outcome: The deal was rejected by 54,000 votes, then revised and passed via Congress.

referendums.name: Fourth term for Morales
referendums.outcome: Voters said no; courts later let him run anyway, and 2019 ended in crisis.

referendums.name: EU migrant quotas
referendums.outcome: An overwhelming No — invalidated by turnout below the 50% threshold.

referendums.name: Marriage equality
referendums.outcome: The first country to legalise same-sex marriage by popular vote.

referendums.name: Bailout terms
referendums.outcome: Greeks rejected the creditors' terms; a harsher deal was signed within weeks.

referendums.name: Single-member districts
referendums.outcome: The lowest turnout in modern European referendum history; legally void.

referendums.name: Scottish independence
referendums.outcome: Scotland stayed in the UK on a record modern turnout.

referendums.name: 'Join Russia'
referendums.outcome: Held under Russian military occupation and recognised by almost no one.
referendums.caveat: A sham vote under occupation; the announced figures are not credible.

referendums.name: Alternative Vote
referendums.outcome: First-past-the-post was retained for Westminster elections.

referendums.name: Keep MMP
referendums.outcome: Voters kept proportional representation.

referendums.name: Independence from Sudan
referendums.outcome: The world's newest state was born that July.

referendums.name: Lisbon Treaty (first vote)
referendums.outcome: Ireland rejected the EU treaty — then approved it 67.1% in 2009 after concessions.

referendums.name: Independence from Serbia
referendums.outcome: Cleared the EU's 55% threshold by half a point.

referendums.name: EU Constitution
referendums.outcome: France sank the constitutional treaty; the Netherlands followed three days later.

referendums.name: EU Constitution
referendums.outcome: The Dutch No, after the French one, killed the treaty.

referendums.name: Adopt the euro
referendums.outcome: Sweden kept the krona.

referendums.name: Adopt the euro
referendums.outcome: Denmark kept the krone.

referendums.name: Republic
referendums.outcome: The monarchy was retained; the proposed model split republicans.

referendums.name: Independence from Indonesia
referendums.outcome: Independence approved amid militia violence; statehood followed in 2002.

referendums.name: Good Friday Agreement
referendums.outcome: Endorsed the peace agreement; the Republic approved it the same day with 94%.

referendums.name: Scottish devolution
referendums.outcome: Created the Scottish Parliament, first elected in 1999.

referendums.name: Quebec sovereignty
referendums.outcome: Canada survived by 54,288 votes — the closest secession vote in a modern democracy.

referendums.name: Divorce
referendums.outcome: Divorce was legalised by nine thousand votes.

referendums.name: EU membership
referendums.outcome: The second No; Norway remains outside the EU.

referendums.name: Adopt MMP
referendums.outcome: Replaced first-past-the-post; the first MMP election followed in 1996.

referendums.name: Form of government
referendums.outcome: Voters kept the republic and chose presidentialism over parliamentarism.

referendums.name: Confidence in Yeltsin
referendums.outcome: Yeltsin won the referendum months before shelling the parliament.

referendums.name: Charlottetown Accord
referendums.outcome: The constitutional package was rejected nationally and in Quebec.

referendums.name: Maastricht Treaty
referendums.outcome: The 'petit oui' that let the euro project proceed.

referendums.name: Maastricht Treaty
referendums.outcome: Denmark's No forced the Edinburgh opt-outs; a second vote passed in 1993.

referendums.name: Join the EEA
referendums.outcome: The narrowest of Nos set Switzerland's bilateral path with Europe.

referendums.name: End apartheid negotiations
referendums.outcome: White voters backed de Klerk's reforms, clearing the road to 1994.
referendums.caveat: The franchise was restricted to white voters.

referendums.name: Preserve the Union
referendums.outcome: Nine months later the USSR was gone — six republics boycotted the vote.

referendums.name: Independence
referendums.outcome: Every region voted yes, including Crimea; the USSR dissolved within the month.

referendums.name: Pinochet's continuation
referendums.outcome: The plebiscite that ended the dictatorship and led to the 1989 elections.

referendums.name: Stay in NATO
referendums.outcome: González reversed his party's stance and won the vote.

referendums.name: Quebec sovereignty-association
referendums.outcome: Quebec's first sovereignty vote failed decisively.

referendums.name: Dictatorship's constitution
referendums.outcome: Uruguayans voted down their own military regime — the beginning of its end.

referendums.name: Scottish devolution
referendums.outcome: A narrow Yes failed the 40%-of-electorate rule; devolution waited 18 years.

referendums.name: Constitution
referendums.outcome: Ratified the democratic constitution after Franco.

referendums.name: EC membership
referendums.outcome: Britain voted to stay in the European Community two years after joining.

referendums.name: Repeal divorce law
referendums.outcome: Italians kept divorce, a landmark defeat for the Christian Democrats.

referendums.name: Republic or monarchy
referendums.outcome: Abolished the monarchy after the junta fell.

referendums.name: EC membership
referendums.outcome: Norway stayed out of Europe — and did it again in 1994.

referendums.name: Women's suffrage
referendums.outcome: Swiss men finally granted women the federal vote.

referendums.name: Senate and regional reform
referendums.outcome: De Gaulle staked his presidency on it and resigned the next day.

referendums.name: Direct presidential election
referendums.outcome: Created the directly elected presidency France still uses.

referendums.name: Republic or monarchy
referendums.outcome: Ended the House of Savoy; the vote that created the Italian Republic.

referendums.name: Republic and severance from Denmark
referendums.outcome: Iceland became a republic on 17 June 1944.

referendums.name: Conscription plebiscite
referendums.outcome: The country said yes — but Quebec voted 72.9% No, a rift that shaped the war years.

referendums.name: Conscription
referendums.outcome: Australians rejected WWI conscription — and again in 1917.
